entityTypes.description: An employee of Corvane Engineering, a fictional mid-sized engineering company. One record per employee; the same real person should not appear twice.

properties.description: Date of birth of the employee.
Company email address; unique per employee.
Personnel number assigned by HR at hiring, in the form E-1234; unique per employee and never reused.
Date and time (UTC) at which the employment started.
Career grade from 1 (entry) to 8 (executive board), as an integer.
Full name of the employee as used in the company directory.
Gross annual salary in euros.
Employment status: "active", "on_leave" or "left".

entityTypes.description: One published version of an internal company policy. A newer version supersedes the previous one; the current version is the one no other version supersedes.

properties.description: Full text of this policy version.
Date on which this version was published.
Title of the policy, the same for all versions of one policy.
Version number of the policy, counting from 1.

entityTypes.description: An internal engineering or business project, owned by one team and staffed by people from any team.

properties.description: Total approved project budget in euros.
Short project code used in time tracking, in the form PRJ-ABC.
Name of the project.
Portfolio priority from 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest), as an integer.
Date on which the project started.
Project status: "planned", "active", "on_hold" or "completed".

entityTypes.description: A professional skill or technology that people have and projects require.

properties.description: Skill area, for example engineering, software, automation, operations, finance or communication.
Seniority band at which the skill is typically expected: "junior", "mid" or "senior". A text value, unlike the integer level of a person.
Name of the skill.

entityTypes.description: An organisational unit of Corvane Engineering with its own cost center. People are members of teams; teams own projects.

properties.description: Annual operating budget of the team in euros.
Accounting cost center code of the team, in the form CC-123.
Name of the team.
Self-assessed proficiency from 1 (basic) to 5 (expert), as an integer.

relationTypes.description: The source person is the direct line manager of the target person.

properties.description: Date from which the reporting line exists.

relationTypes.description: The person belongs to the team, with a role and a share of working time.

properties.description: Share of the person's working time spent in this team, from 0.0 to 1.0.
Job role of the person within the team.

relationTypes.description: The team responsible for the project.
The project needs people with the skill.
The source policy version replaces the target policy version, which is the version immediately before it.
The person is staffed on the project.

properties.description: Planned working hours per week on the project.

lenses.name: All
lenses.description: Unscoped lens over the whole organisation graph: people, teams, projects, skills and policy documents with every relation.

aiAgents.name: Org Analyst
aiAgents.description: Answers questions about people, teams, projects and skills of Corvane Engineering using saved queries and read-only OQL.
aiAgents.systemPrompt: You answer questions about the organisation of Corvane Engineering: reporting lines, team membership, project staffing, skills and policy versions. Prefer a saved query: find it with search_saved_queries or list_saved_queries and run it with run_saved_query. When no saved query fits, read the schema with get_schema and write one read-only OQL query with execute_query, using type keys and labelled node patterns. Name the people, teams and projects your answer is based on.

savedQueries.name: Average Salary Per Team
savedQueries.description: Average annual salary and member count of every team. A person in two teams counts in both; people without a salary count as members but not in the average.

steps.name: main
steps.oql: MATCH (p:person)-[:member_of]->(t:team) RETURN t.name AS team, avg(p.salary) AS average_salary, count(p) AS members ORDER BY team

savedQueries.name: Direct Reports Per Manager
savedQueries.description: Counts the direct reports of every manager (people with at least one outgoing manages relation), largest span of control first.

steps.name: main
steps.oql: MATCH (m:person)-[:manages]->(r:person) RETURN m.name AS manager, count(r) AS direct_reports ORDER BY direct_reports DESC, manager

savedQueries.name: Persons Hired After
savedQueries.description: People whose employment started after a given date, most recent hire first.

steps.name: main
steps.oql: MATCH (p:person) WHERE p.hired_at > $since RETURN p.name AS person, p.hired_at AS hired_at, p.level AS level ORDER BY hired_at DESC

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Cut-off date (YYYY-MM-DD); people hired after it are returned.

savedQueries.name: Persons With Projects
savedQueries.description: Every person with the projects they work on and their weekly hours, including people who work on no project (project and hours are then empty).

steps.name: main
steps.oql: MATCH (p:person) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[w:works_on]->(j:project) RETURN p.name AS person, p.employee_number AS employee_number, j.name AS project, w.hours_per_week AS hours ORDER BY person, employee_number, project

savedQueries.name: Projects With Minimum Priority
savedQueries.description: Projects whose priority is at least the given value (1 lowest to 5 highest), highest priority first.

steps.name: main
steps.oql: MATCH (p:project) WHERE p.priority >= $min_priority RETURN p.name AS project, p.code AS code, p.priority AS priority, p.status AS status ORDER BY priority DESC, project

parameters.name: min_priority
parameters.description: Minimum priority, an integer from 1 to 5.

savedQueries.name: Skill Holders By Team
savedQueries.description: Finds skills matching a search text, then the people who have them, then groups those people by team. Three steps: search over skills, people with those skills, their teams.

steps.name: holders
steps.oql: MATCH (p:person)-[h:has_skill]->(s:skill) WHERE s._id IN $skill_ids RETURN p._id AS person_id, p.name AS person, s.name AS skill, h.proficiency AS proficiency ORDER BY person

steps.name: teams
steps.oql: MATCH (p:person)-[:member_of]->(t:team) WHERE p._id IN $person_ids RETURN t.name AS team, count(p) AS holders, collect(p.name) AS people ORDER BY holders DESC, team

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search text naming a skill, for example "Rust" or "PLC".

savedQueries.name: Skills For Team Projects
savedQueries.description: Lists the skills required by the projects a given team owns, each skill with the projects that need it. Two hops: team <- owned_by - project - requires_skill -> skill.

steps.name: main
steps.oql: MATCH (t:team)<-[:owned_by]-(p:project)-[:requires_skill]->(s:skill) WHERE t.name = $team RETURN s.name AS skill, collect(p.name) AS projects ORDER BY skill

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: Exact team name, for example "Hardware Engineering".

lenses.name: Directory
lenses.description: Company directory: people and teams only. Relations are inferred (manages, member_of). Salary and birth date are hidden.

lenses.name: Management
lenses.description: Reporting lines and team membership: people and teams with the manages and member_of relations; the allocation of a membership is hidden.

lenses.name: Staffing
lenses.description: Staffing view: every entity type, but only the works_on, has_skill and requires_skill relations.
